stages.title: Sounds and musical instruments
stages.hook: Put your hand on your throat and hum. What do you feel? Where does the sound come from?
explain: Sound starts when something shakes very fast. We call this shaking a vibration. You cannot always see it, but you can feel it.
A musical instrument is a thing that makes sound on purpose. You can hit a drum. You can pluck a string on a guitar. You can blow into a flute. You can shake a shaker.
Your voice is an instrument too. It lives inside you!

example.q: How does a drum make a sound?
steps: The shaking moves the air and reaches your ear.
example.a: The drum skin vibrates (shakes) and we hear it.

analogies.home: Pluck a rubber band stretched on a box. It wobbles and you hear a buzzy note.
analogies.farm: A cowbell rings when the cow walks, because the bell shakes.
analogies.sea: Waves make a swishing sound when water moves back and forth.
analogies.music: A drum, a shaker and a flute all make sound by shaking in different ways.

stages.mnemonic: Shake, shake, sound! No shake, no sound.
terms: What we hear when something shakes.
Something we use to make music.

misc.wrong: Only things from a shop can make music.
misc.right: Many things can make music. Spoons, pots, hands and your voice all can.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. Find one you hit, one you blow and one you pluck.

questions.q: What does a sound need to start?
questions.why: Sound is made when something vibrates, or shakes.

questions.q: How do you play a drum?
questions.why: A drum makes sound when you hit its skin.

questions.q: How do you play a flute?
questions.why: A flute makes sound when air is blown across it.

questions.q: You touch a guitar string while it makes a sound. What do you feel?
questions.why: A sounding string vibrates, so you can feel the shaking.

questions.q: Is your voice an instrument?
o: No, only things in shops are instruments
Yes, it makes sound by shaking inside your throat
questions.why: Your voice box vibrates when you sing, so your voice is an instrument.

questions.q: Match the instrument to how we play it.
questions.why: Each instrument is played in its own way.

questions.q: A bell rings. Then you hold it tight and it goes quiet. Why?
o: The bell got too tired to ring
questions.why: No shaking means no sound. Your hand stopped the vibration.

questions.q: Which of these can make music?
o: A stone that is not touched
questions.why: Tapping spoons makes them shake, so they make sound and can be played.

questions.q: Which is NOT an instrument?
questions.why: A pillow does not make a clear sound when played.

questions.q: Put these in order: how a drum makes sound.
questions.why: Hit, then shake, then moving air, then hearing.

panel.q: Why can music be made with just a table and your hands?
o: The table shakes when you tap it, so it makes sound
Hands are magic and need no table
panel.why: Anything that shakes when tapped can make sound.

panel.q: Two drums. One is big and one is small. Both are hit. Why might they sound different?
o: One drum is feeling shy today
panel.why: Size changes how things shake, so the sound changes.

panel.q: You hear a sound in the next room. What must be true?
panel.why: All sounds come from vibrations.

teach.model: Sound comes when something shakes. A drum skin shakes when you hit it. The shaking moves the air and we hear it. A guitar and a flute shake too, in their own ways.

points.ask: What happens to the thing that makes the sound?
Can you tell me one instrument?
How does the sound get to us?

stages.title: High and low pitch
stages.hook: A tiny bird sings. A big bear growls. Which one has the higher sound?
explain: Pitch tells us how high or low a sound is. A bird tweet is high. A lion roar is low.
Small things often make high sounds. Big things often make low sounds. A small drum sounds higher than a big drum.
Pitch is not the same as loud. A high sound can be very quiet. A low sound can be very loud.

example.q: Which is lower: a mouse squeak or a cow moo?
steps: Think of the mouse. Its squeak is thin and high.
Think of the cow. Its moo is deep.

analogies.home: Little feet go tip-tap, high. Big boots go thud, low.
analogies.farm: A chick says peep, high. A cow says moo, low.
analogies.nature: A cricket chirps high. Thunder rumbles low.
analogies.music: On a piano, keys on the right sound high. Keys on the left sound low.

stages.mnemonic: Little and light, high as a kite. Big and deep, low as a sheep.
terms: How high or low a sound is.
A thin, small sound, like a bird.
A deep, big sound, like a bear.
One musical sound with a pitch.

misc.right: High means a thin sound. It can be loud or quiet. Loud is a different thing.

trip.prompt: Look for a picture of a piano. Which end is high? Which end is low?

questions.q: Which animal makes the higher sound?
questions.why: Small animals often make high sounds.

questions.q: Listen. Is the second note higher or lower than the first?
questions.why: The second note, 72, is higher than the first, 60.

questions.q: Listen again. Is the second note higher or lower than the first?
questions.why: The second note, 55, is lower than the first, 67.

questions.q: Listen. Are the two notes the same or different?
questions.why: Both notes are 64, so they are the same.

questions.q: What word tells us how high or low a sound is?
questions.why: Pitch means high or low.

questions.q: On a piano, which keys play the high notes?
questions.why: Moving right on a piano makes the notes higher.

questions.q: Match each sound to its pitch.
questions.why: Tiny things squeak high. Big things rumble low. Two matching notes have the same pitch.

questions.q: A tiny whistle and a big tuba play. Which is probably lower?
questions.why: Big instruments usually make lower sounds.

questions.q: Is a quiet mouse squeak high or low?
o: Low, because it is so quiet
It has no pitch at all
High, even though it is quiet
questions.why: Pitch and loudness are different.

questions.q: Put these sounds from lowest to highest.
questions.why: Deep sounds come first and thin sounds come last.

panel.q: A friend says "that note is high, so it must be loud". What do you say?
o: Only low notes can be quiet
High and loud are different things
panel.why: Pitch is high or low. Loudness is how strong a sound is.

panel.q: You hear notes going 60, 64, 67 on a keyboard. Which way do they go?
panel.why: The numbers rise, so the pitch goes up.

panel.q: Why is a baby sound often higher than a grown-up sound?
o: Smaller voice boxes make higher sounds
Babies do not need to breathe
panel.why: Small things shake fast and sound higher.

teach.model: Pitch means how high or low a sound is. A bird sings high and a bear growls low. Small things often sound high and big things sound low. It is not the same as loud.

points.ask: And what is a low sound?
Can you give me an example?
Is high the same as loud?

stages.title: Loud and soft sounds
stages.hook: How do you say hello to a baby who is sleeping? How do you call a friend far away? Is your voice the same?
explain: Sounds can be loud or soft. We call this dynamics. Loud sounds are strong. Soft sounds are gentle.
In music, loud can feel big and brave. Soft can feel calm and sleepy. A lullaby is soft. A parade drum is loud.
Players change from soft to loud on purpose. It makes the music feel alive.

example.q: Which is better for a bedtime song: loud or soft?
steps: A bedtime song helps you sleep.

analogies.home: You whisper in the library and shout in the garden.
analogies.city: A car horn is loud. A cat walking is soft.
analogies.sport: A crowd cheers loud when a goal is scored and goes quiet at a penalty kick.
analogies.nature: A storm is loud. Falling snow is soft.

stages.mnemonic: Soft as a feather, loud as a drum.
terms: How loud or soft music is.

misc.right: Music can be very soft too. Many songs change from soft to loud.

trip.prompt: Look for the words that mean loud and soft in music.

questions.q: What do we call how loud or soft music is?
questions.why: Dynamics are the loud and soft parts of music.

questions.q: Which song is usually soft?
questions.why: Lullabies help babies sleep, so they are gentle.

questions.q: A drum is hit very gently. How does it sound?
questions.why: A gentle tap makes a soft sound.

questions.q: A drum is hit very hard. How does it sound?
questions.why: Hitting harder shakes it more, so it sounds louder.

questions.q: You want to hear a quiet bird. What should the room be like?
questions.why: Loud sounds hide soft sounds.

questions.q: Match the thing to loud or soft.
pairs: How loud or soft music is
questions.why: Thunder is strong and loud. A whisper is soft. Dynamics is the word for loud and soft.

questions.q: Put these from softest to loudest.
questions.why: Each sound is stronger than the one before.

questions.q: A song starts soft and gets louder and louder. What happens to the feeling?
o: It gets more sleepy and slow
It gets bigger and more exciting
questions.why: Getting louder builds excitement.

questions.q: Why do players sometimes play soft on purpose?
o: To make music gentle or calm
questions.why: Soft playing is a choice to change the feeling.

questions.q: Is a quiet sound always a low sound?
o: No, a quiet sound can be high or low
Yes, if it is a bird
questions.why: Loudness and pitch are different.

panel.q: Why do people whisper in a library?
o: Because libraries are made of wood
So others can read in peace
panel.why: Soft sounds do not bother others.

panel.q: A band plays soft, then a big loud crash. What does the crash do?
o: It makes the music go slower
It surprises us and gets our attention
It changes the key of the song
panel.why: A sudden loud sound is a surprise.

panel.q: A shaker is shaken harder. What changes?
panel.why: More energy makes more sound.

teach.model: Music can be loud or soft. We use soft for calm songs like lullabies and loud for big, strong songs like parades. We change it on purpose to make a feeling.

stages.title: Rhythm and clapping
stages.hook: Clap your hands to your favourite song. Did you clap in a steady way? What is that steady thing?
explain: Music has a beat. The beat is like a steady heartbeat: boom, boom, boom, boom. You can march or tap to it.
Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds over the beat. Clap-clap-clap-clap is all the same. Clap, clap-clap, clap is a rhythm with long and short sounds.
Every country has rhythms that people clap, stomp or drum. Rhythm is something you can do with just your body.

example.q: A rhythm is clap, clap-clap, clap. How many claps in all?
steps: Count the two quick claps: 2 more makes 3.

analogies.home: A clock goes tick, tick, tick. That is a steady beat.
analogies.sport: Marching feet keep the beat. A drum pattern keeps a rhythm.
analogies.nature: Rain on a roof goes pitter-patter in a pattern.
analogies.music: The bass drum keeps the beat. The shaker plays little fast rhythms.

stages.mnemonic: Beat is the heart. Rhythm is the dance.
terms: A pattern of long and short sounds.
A sound you make with your hands.
Another word for the steady beat.

misc.wrong: Beat and rhythm are exactly the same.
misc.right: The beat is steady. The rhythm is the pattern on top of the beat.

trip.prompt: Find a picture of someone playing a drum. Can you tap along in your mind?

questions.q: What is the steady pulse in music called?
questions.why: The beat is steady like a heartbeat.

questions.q: What is a pattern of long and short sounds called?
questions.why: Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds.

questions.q: Listen to the rhythm. How many sounds do you hear?
questions.why: The rhythm has 4 claps: long, short, short, long.

questions.q: Listen. How many claps do you hear?
questions.why: There are five claps.

questions.q: Which one keeps going like a heartbeat?
questions.why: The beat is steady.

questions.q: You march left, right, left, right. What are your feet keeping?
questions.why: Steady steps show the beat.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.why: Each word has its own job.

questions.q: Why is it easy to dance to a steady beat?
o: You always know when the next step comes
The beat changes all the time
The beat is a bright colour
questions.why: A steady beat is easy to follow.

questions.q: Two kids clap the same beat. One claps a fast rhythm. One claps a slow rhythm. What is the same?
questions.why: The beat stays steady while the rhythm changes.

questions.q: Can you make rhythm with no instrument?
o: Yes, with hands, feet or voice
questions.why: Your body can clap, stomp and tap.

panel.q: A friend says the beat and the rhythm are always the same. Is that true?
o: No, the rhythm can have long and short sounds while the beat stays even
Yes, rhythm is just a colour
panel.why: Rhythm is a pattern on top of the beat.

panel.q: Why do many people around the world use drums?
o: Drums make strong rhythms and beats that people can feel
Drums are cheap and easy to buy
Drums have no sound at all
Only kings are allowed to use drums
panel.why: Drums are used in music in every part of the world.

panel.q: Why does a clock feel steady?
o: It has no sound at all
It plays long and short sounds
It ticks at the same speed each time
panel.why: Equal gaps make a steady beat.

teach.model: The beat is the steady pulse like a heartbeat. Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds. You can clap a rhythm while your feet keep the beat.

stages.title: Fast and slow tempo
stages.hook: A snail walks. A cheetah runs. How might music sound if it moved like each of them?
explain: Tempo means how fast or slow the beat goes. A fast tempo is quick like a rabbit. A slow tempo is calm like a snail.
Fast music often feels happy and busy. Slow music often feels calm. But not always! A fast song can still be sad, and a slow one can be happy.
Players can speed up or slow down on purpose. A conductor can guide the tempo with a stick or hands.

example.q: A song has 60 beats in one minute. Another has 120. Which is faster?
steps: More beats in one minute means faster.

analogies.home: You walk slowly in the dark and run when you are late.
analogies.sport: A jogger runs slow. A sprinter races fast.
analogies.farm: A tortoise goes slowly. A horse gallops fast.
analogies.nature: A river trickles slow, then rushes fast after rain.

terms: How fast or slow the beat is.
A person who guides players with their hands.

misc.right: Tempo is only speed. A fast song can feel sad and a slow song can feel happy.

trip.prompt: Find the words people use for fast and slow. Which one is Allegro?

questions.q: What word means how fast or slow the beat goes?
questions.why: Tempo is speed of the beat.

questions.q: Listen. Is this rhythm fast or slow?
questions.why: Eight quick sounds are played in the time of two beats, so it is fast.

questions.q: Now listen to this one. Is it fast or slow?
questions.why: Each sound lasts two whole beats, so it feels slow.

questions.q: Which animal is a good match for a slow tempo?
questions.why: A snail moves slowly.

questions.q: Which animal is a good match for a fast tempo?
questions.why: A rabbit runs quickly.

questions.q: Which song speed would suit a calm bedtime?
questions.why: A slow tempo helps people feel calm.

questions.q: Match each one to what goes with it.
questions.why: A rabbit is quick and a snail is slow. A conductor guides the players and the tempo.

questions.q: Put these from slowest to fastest.
questions.why: Each moves faster than the one before.

questions.q: Song A has 70 beats a minute. Song B has 140. Which is slower?
questions.why: Fewer beats a minute means slower.

questions.q: A band is playing a slow song, then speeds up. What does the music feel like?
questions.why: Speeding up adds energy.

panel.q: Can a fast song be sad?
o: No, fast songs are always happy
Yes, tempo and feeling are different things
Only if it is very loud
panel.why: Mood comes from many things, not only tempo.

panel.q: Why do dancers like a clear tempo?
o: It hides the beat from them
They know how fast to move
panel.why: The tempo tells them how fast to step.

panel.q: What does a conductor help the players with?
o: Playing together at the same tempo
Being louder than all the others
Hiding the beat from the crowd
panel.why: A conductor helps everyone stay together.

teach.model: Tempo is how fast or slow the beat goes. A rabbit is fast and a snail is slow. Slow music often feels calm and fast music often feels busy, but not always.

points.ask: Can you give me a picture of each?
How does it make music feel?

stages.title: Recognising melodies
stages.hook: Think of a song you love. Can you hum it without any words? What are you humming?
explain: A melody is the tune of a song. It is a line of notes that go up, down or stay the same. It is the part you hum.
Some melodies jump. Some melodies walk step by step. Some melodies go up, up, up. Some go down, down, down.
Songs from all over the world have melodies that people remember. Listening carefully helps you know a tune when you hear it again.

example.q: A tune goes C, D, E. Does it go up or down?
steps: D is higher than C. E is higher than D.
Each note is higher than the one before.

analogies.home: You know mum or dad by the way they walk. You know a song by its tune.
analogies.city: A phone ring has a short tune you know at once.
analogies.sea: Waves rise and fall like a melody going up and down.
analogies.music: Humming gives the melody with no words.

stages.mnemonic: Hum it, that is the melody!
terms: To sing a tune with your mouth closed.

misc.right: The melody is the notes. The words can change but the melody can stay.

trip.prompt: Find a short tune on the page. Can you tell if it goes up or down?

questions.q: What do we call the tune of a song?
questions.why: The melody is the tune.

questions.q: Listen. Do the notes go up, down or stay the same?
questions.why: The notes 60, 62, 64 climb higher.

questions.q: Listen again. Do the notes go up, down or stay the same?
questions.why: The notes 67, 64, 60 get lower.

questions.q: One more time. Do these notes go up, down or stay the same?
questions.why: All three notes are 60.

questions.q: How can you share a tune with no words?
questions.why: Humming gives the notes of the melody.

questions.q: Two songs have different words but the same notes. What is the same?
questions.why: The melody is the notes.

questions.q: Match the tune shape to the word.
questions.why: Melody shapes are up, down or same.

questions.q: Put these notes in order so the melody goes up.
questions.why: Each note is higher than the one before: C, D, E, F.

questions.q: You hear a tune on the radio but it has no words. How do you know it?
o: By the time on the clock
questions.why: You know it by the tune.

questions.q: Which is part of a song you can hum?
questions.why: The melody is the hummable part.

panel.q: Why can people from different countries enjoy the same melody?
o: It always has the same words
It is only meant for kings
A melody does not need words to be understood
panel.why: Notes can be enjoyed without language.

panel.q: A tune goes 72, 67, 64, 60. What is its shape?
panel.why: Each note is lower than the last.

panel.q: Why do lullabies often have gentle, smooth melodies?
o: To hide the beat from them
To be very loud and bold
panel.why: Smooth, soft tunes are calming.

teach.model: A melody is the tune of a song, the part you can hum. It is made of notes that go up, down or stay the same. You can know a song by its tune even without words.

points.ask: Can you tell me a song with a melody?
Do we need words to know a melody?

stages.title: Singing simple songs
stages.hook: Take a big breath in. Now sing one long "la". How does your body help you sing?
explain: Singing uses your voice, your breath and your listening ears. Sit or stand tall so the air can move. Breathe in low into your tummy.
Sing softly at first. Do not shout. Drink water to keep your voice happy. If your throat hurts, rest.
Many songs are easy and have only a few notes. Songs for children, work songs and lullabies exist in every part of the world. Singing with friends is fun.

example.q: What should you do before singing?
example.a: Stand tall, breathe in, and start softly.

analogies.home: You sing in the bath and it sounds big and echoing.
analogies.farm: People sing while they work to keep a steady beat.
analogies.sport: Fans sing together to cheer on their team.
analogies.sea: Sailors long ago sang work songs to pull ropes together.

stages.mnemonic: Tall back, big breath, soft start.
terms: The air you take in and let out.
To make music with your voice.
Gentle practice before a big job.

misc.wrong: You sing best when you shout.
misc.right: Shouting hurts your voice. Calm, relaxed singing sounds better.

trip.prompt: Find a picture of a choir. How are the singers standing?

questions.q: What should you do before you sing?
questions.why: Breath gives your voice air.

questions.q: How should you stand or sit to sing?
questions.why: A tall back lets the air move freely.

questions.q: Your throat feels sore. What is best?
questions.why: Rest helps a sore voice get better.

questions.q: What is a group of singers called?
questions.why: A choir sings together.

questions.q: Is a voice an instrument?
questions.why: Voices make sound by vibrating.

questions.q: Match the word to the meaning.
questions.why: Each word names a part of singing.

questions.q: You sing a high note and your throat feels tight. What could help?
o: Try again gently with a calm breath
questions.why: Relaxed singing is safer and sounds better.

questions.q: Why do work songs help people do a job together?
o: They hide the noise of work
They give a steady beat to work to
questions.why: A beat helps people move at the same time.

questions.q: Put these in a good order for singing.
questions.why: First your body, then breath, then sound.

questions.q: Why is singing with friends fun?
o: You share music and sound together
You must not smile at all
questions.why: Singing together is a shared joy.

panel.q: Why should you sing softly at first?
o: It keeps your voice safe and warm
So that no one can hear you
It is a rule for drum players
panel.why: Easy starts protect your voice.

panel.q: Why do people in all countries sing lullabies?
o: Gentle songs help children calm and sleep
panel.why: Slow soft singing is calming.

panel.q: A song has just three notes. Is it still a real song?
o: No, it needs more notes than that

Yes, simple songs are real songs
Only if a choir sings it
panel.why: Many songs use few notes.

teach.model: To sing, sit or stand tall and take a calm breath. Start softly and do not shout. Rest and drink water if your throat is sore. Singing with friends is fun.

points.ask: How loud should I be at the start?
How do I look after my voice?

stages.title: Musical patterns
stages.hook: Look at a pattern of bricks, stripes or tiles. Does something repeat? Can music repeat too?
explain: A pattern is something that repeats. Red, blue, red, blue is a pattern. In music, rhythms, notes and whole tunes can repeat.
We use letters to show patterns. A B A B means: first sound, second sound, first sound, second sound. AABB and ABA are different patterns.
When a pattern repeats, your ear knows what to expect. When it changes, you notice. That makes music fun to follow.

example.q: A pattern goes clap, stomp, clap, stomp. What comes next?
steps: Look at the pattern: clap, stomp, clap, stomp.

analogies.home: Plates on a table: big, small, big, small.
analogies.city: Zebra crossing stripes: white, black, white, black.
analogies.nature: Waves come in again and again.
analogies.music: A drum goes boom, tap, boom, tap.

stages.mnemonic: Same again? That is a pattern, friend!
terms: A part of a song that repeats with new words.

misc.right: Patterns help us follow music and feel the fun of surprises when they change.

trip.prompt: Look for one pattern in the picture. Can you name it with letters?

questions.q: What is a pattern?
o: A single thing that never repeats
questions.why: A pattern repeats.

questions.q: Clap, stomp, clap, stomp, clap, ... What comes next?
questions.why: The pattern alternates clap and stomp.

questions.q: Which is the pattern A B A B?
questions.why: A and B take turns: boom tap boom tap.

questions.q: What does it mean to echo?
questions.why: An echo repeats a sound.

questions.q: Which pattern has all different parts?
questions.why: Every letter is different.

questions.q: The pattern is clap clap stomp, clap clap stomp, clap clap stomp. How many stomps?
questions.why: Each group of three has one stomp, and there are three groups.

questions.q: Match the letters to the sounds. A = clap, B = stomp.
questions.why: Replace each letter by its sound.

questions.q: Why do patterns help us enjoy music?
o: We can guess what comes next
They hide the tune from us
questions.why: The ear likes to expect and follow.

questions.q: The pattern is clap clap stomp, clap clap ... What comes next?
questions.why: The pattern is clap clap stomp, so after clap clap comes stomp.

questions.q: A song comes back to the same chorus after each verse. What is that?
questions.why: Returning parts make a pattern.

panel.q: Why do many songs repeat the chorus?
o: The singer simply forgot the rest
It makes them easy to remember and sing along to
To make the song much shorter
To hide the tune from people
panel.why: Repetition helps memory.

panel.q: A pattern goes A B A B. Someone changes the last B to C. What happens?
panel.why: A change in a pattern stands out.

panel.q: Can a pattern be made of rhythms and notes together?
panel.why: Music patterns can use any sounds.

teach.model: A pattern is a thing that repeats. In music a rhythm, a tune or a whole part can repeat. We can use letters like A B A B to show it. Patterns help us follow and enjoy music.

points.ask: Can you give a music example?
How can we write a pattern?

stages.title: Introduction to musical genres
stages.hook: Do people in every country make music? Does it all sound the same?
explain: A genre is a kind or style of music. Pop is catchy songs on the radio. Rock uses loud guitars and drums. Jazz often has players who make up music as they go. Classical often uses orchestras.

Different places have their own music too. Reggae comes from Jamaica. Samba comes from Brazil. Highlife grew up in West Africa. Flamenco comes from Spain. Country music is popular in the United States.
There is no best genre. Each is a way to share feelings and stories. Listening to many kinds helps us enjoy more of the world.

steps: Think of a laid-back beat that people dance to.

analogies.home: You have favourite foods and favourite music. Each is a style you like.
analogies.city: A big city can have many music styles, from street drums to concert halls.
analogies.farm: Country songs often talk about open land and daily life.
analogies.music: Each genre is like a different flavour of ice cream.

stages.mnemonic: Many genres, many ways to say it with sound.
terms: A kind or style of music.
Catchy songs that many people like.
Music where players make up parts as they play.
Music from Jamaica with a relaxed, offbeat rhythm.

misc.right: Each genre has its own beauty. Different people enjoy different music.

trip.prompt: Find three genres on the list that you have not heard of.

questions.q: What is a genre?
questions.why: A genre is a style or kind of music.

questions.q: Which genre began in Jamaica?
questions.why: Reggae grew up in Jamaica.

questions.q: Which genre is linked with Brazil and carnival?
questions.why: Samba is linked with Brazil.

questions.q: Which genre is linked with Spain?
questions.why: Flamenco comes from southern Spain.

questions.q: Which genre often has an orchestra?
questions.why: Orchestras are often used in classical music.

questions.q: Match the genre to a place it is linked with.
questions.why: Each genre grew in a region.

questions.q: A friend likes one genre. You like another. What is true?
questions.why: Taste is personal.

questions.q: You hear loud guitars and strong drums. Which genre is it likely to be?
questions.why: Rock is known for electric guitars and drums.

questions.q: Why is it good to listen to many genres?
o: To make them all sound the same
To stay away from new things

questions.why: Music is a way to meet other cultures.

questions.q: Music where the players make up parts as they play is often called what?
questions.why: Improvising is common in jazz.

panel.q: Why do so many places have their own music?
o: They are told to by the king
People make music about their own lives and share it
Only one place is allowed to have music
panel.why: Music grows from people and place.

panel.q: Can two genres borrow ideas from each other?
panel.why: Genres change and blend over time.

panel.q: A song is called pop. What does that most likely mean?
o: It is a drum and nothing else
It is a very quiet song
It is a very old folk song

panel.why: Pop is short for popular.

teach.model: A genre is a kind or style of music. Pop, rock, jazz, classical, reggae and samba are all genres. They come from different places and people. There is no best one.

points.ask: Is one better than the others?
